paper.title: Algorithm 693: A FORTRAN package for floating-point multiple-precision arithmetic
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 17(2), June 1991, pp. 273-283 (volume, issue and pages from the archive header; article not read, ACM pages return 403 from this sandbox)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 693.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into /tmp/scout-693 as 693.raw, read as text, not executed)
code.archive: netlib TOMS 693.gz, single Fortran source file 9743 lines, FM 1.0 by David M Smith (1990)
code.note: The file is the complete package with a self-checking driver: PROGRAM TEST (line 9534) and subroutine CHECK. The rerun must compile the whole file with a Fortran 77 compiler, run the program, and compare TEST.OUT with the expected values written in the program's own header comment (lines 9534-9600, the 'output from this program should be' block) and in its RESULT strings.

claim.location: The expected output block in the header comment of PROGRAM TEST in 693.gz (the entry 'SQRT(3) =' at 40 decimal places), which the program also checks itself through RESULT and CHECK. The program calls FPI2M, FPSQRT and FPPRNT with 40 significant digits set by FPSET(40).

reference.file: PROGRAM TEST header comment and RESULT string in 693.gz (TEST routine, lines 9534-9600)
reference.sha256: not recorded: text read from the netlib shar; rerun should compare the member

claim.metric: Decimal digits of sqrt(3) produced by FPSQRT on FPI2M(3) and printed by FPPRNT with JFORM2=40 (fixed point, 40 places).
claim.paper_value: Shipped reference: 1.7320508075688772935274463415058723669428 (the paper itself is not read here).

tolerance.basis: The reference has 40 decimal places, so its rounding half-unit in the last place is 5e-41. The driver's own CHECK compares the printed 80-character string exactly, which is stricter. Set before any run and not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one compile and a handful of FM operations.
cost.data_licence: No data. Public netlib TOMS archive.

why: sqrt(3) to 40 digits needs the package's extended-precision square root, so the printed digits test the port of the method rather than a value the reader can write down.
